analysis.title: Mizuho FICC Focus: UK Labour Mkt Data, Inflation data, FOMC Minutes, Japan GDP (13 November 2026)
key_insights: Mizuho expects the Fed to hike twice (Dec 2026 and Mar 2027) with risks skewed toward a faster cycle. ECB hikes once more in Dec then holds. BoE hikes in Nov and Mar. BoJ hikes in Dec, Mar and Jun to a 2.00% terminal rate.

Mizuho sees limited room for a sustained duration rally. US 10yr near 5% looks broadly fair, EUR yields should resume their rise into year-end, and Gilts are preferred because of lower long-end supply. Curves may stay flatter near term, with re-steepening in 2027 except in JGBs.

FX view: USD stays rangebound into year-end and strengthens in 2027 on better US growth and higher yields. Mizuho is bearish EUR/USD into 2027, expects GBP to be better supported by improving growth, and sees JPY as structurally weak despite further BoJ tightening.

Inflation risks are skewed higher, especially in the US. Europe and the UK are exposed to energy, but second-round effects look contained so far. Higher oil is the main global upside risk. Key uncertainties listed are US-Iran, UK politics, EUR elections and AI.

The week opened after an equity selloff that followed a hotter CPI, then a PPI that Mizuho calls a non-event. Next week's data calendar is light, with attention on the UK (labour market 17 Nov, CPI 18 Nov) and Japan (Q3 GDP, national CPI 20 Nov in the week table, 19 Nov in the event list, and a BOJ Takata speech 16 Nov).

UK labour market: PAYE data shows consistent job losses and rising unemployment, and surveys point to weak hiring and wage growth. Mizuho's slack metric shows a loose labour market that should limit aggressive wage growth, though some wage indicators remain sticky. If wage data slows, the BoE may be less keen to hike in December.
UK headline CPI and inflation momentum have accelerated, driven by goods. Services inflation, which the BoE watches most, shows no major pickup so far.

ECB succession: Lagarde steps down 7 February, Schnabel leaves for the IMF in January and Lane's term ends in May, so three of six Executive Board seats change within five months. A Knot presidency would probably be read as somewhat more hawkish at first, mainly at the front end. One discussed package has Knot as President, France taking Chief Economist and Germany keeping a Board seat. Spain's absence from that package could strengthen Hernández de Cos. The hawkish or dovish read depends on the whole package, including who replaces Schnabel.

FX positioning: CFTC non-commercial USD longs have retraced somewhat but remain very bullish on the dollar. EURGBP implied vols eased again and USDJPY implied vols fell. Mizuho notes a Democratic sweep in the midterms may be bullish EUR FX, and says it is too early to say vol risk has passed.

US-Iran: Mizuho's narrative-shift index (z-scores of 10Y UST yields and Brent) points to risk of escalation after the US midterms. Brent tested $90/bbl this week and stayed below $100. Inventories are drawing down and Strait traffic is severely compromised.

Mizuho US-Iran scenario odds: proxy escalation 40%, hard-line US response 30%, strategic patience 25%, limited transaction deal 5%. Proxy escalation means Brent spikes above $90 and rates become more sensitive to crude. A hard-line response means Brent sustainably above $90 with spikes above $100, and bear-flattening. Strategic patience means Brent in a $75-90 range, where Mizuho says to fade oil rallies. A deal means Brent below $75 and a bull-flattener that turns into a bull-steepener.

Supply for the week of 16-20 Nov: USTs have negative net supply of $91.2bn (20Y bond $16bn, 10Y TIPS $19bn). Bunds net +EUR 8bn, OATs +EUR 11.25-13.75bn, BTPs zero, SPGBs +EUR 6bn, Gilts +GBP 3.4bn. Calendar-year-to-date issuance completion is 87.2% for the first chart market, 93.3%, 97%, 92%, 83% and 84% for the others, in the order shown.

Mizuho's trade ideas: long 2Y USD swap spreads, boxed 5s30s UK flatteners vs US steepeners, short German 15Y ASW vs long 7Y ASW, SFIZ6Z7 steepener, short 10yr SONIA on 5s10s30s, pay USDJPY 2y3y XCCY basis, and long 20yr JGB on a 10s20s30s fly.

Stops and targets were revised on three trades: the USD swap spread stop to -18bps, the German ASW stop to 21.5bp, the USDJPY XCCY basis stop to -31bp (the summary slide lists -34bp), and the JGB fly stop to 66bp with target 50bp.

Broader risks Mizuho lists include an AI capex debt wall, private credit cracks spreading to banks, a Blue Wave raising US fiscal and term premium risk, a stablecoin run hitting T-bills, French OAT-Bund widening, NATO fiscal expansion, and an energy shock derailing Europe or forcing the BoJ into a trade-off.

trade_ideas.description: Long 2Y USD swap spreads. Entry -23.6bps, target -10bp, stop -18bps.
trade_ideas.rationale: The eSLR change was confirmed and further deregulation could incentivise banks to buy more Treasuries.
trade_ideas.risk: No regulatory follow-through or only minor tweaks to the SLR, or higher than expected US fiscal spending.

trade_ideas.description: Boxed 5s30s UK flatteners vs US steepeners. Entry 20bps, target 0bps, stop 30bps.
trade_ideas.rationale: UK fiscal prudence and less long-end gilt supply versus persistent US fiscal concerns and Democratic spending.
trade_ideas.risk: UK term premium rises on fiscal or inflation deterioration, the trade struggles if Democrats deliver tax-and-spend compromises, or a sharp US growth slowdown lets duration demand overwhelm.

trade_ideas.description: Short German 15Y ASW vs long 7Y German ASW. Entry 21bp, target 29bp, stop 21.5bp.
trade_ideas.rationale: Solid growth momentum and higher German issuance should steepen curves, and the 7Y point is undertapped versus the 15Y area.
trade_ideas.risk: Global flattening momentum, underwhelming German issuance, or higher 7Y issuance in the Q2 refunding.

trade_ideas.description: SFIZ6Z7 steepener (GBP STIR). Entry 0.03bp, target 0.75bp, stop 0.50bp.
trade_ideas.rationale: Listed as a high-conviction trade idea with no rationale slide in this deck.

trade_ideas.description: Short 10yr SONIA on 5s10s30s. Entry 16.1bp, target 8bp, stop 17.5bp, carry and roll -0.6bp/month.

trade_ideas.description: Pay USDJPY 2y3y XCCY basis. Entry -32.4bp, target -29bp, stop -31bp (revised), carry and roll 0.3bp/month.
trade_ideas.rationale: Benign funding conditions, positive risk sentiment, quiet supply, appetite to buy JPY credit swapped and a lack of receiving flow from Japan point to better paying.

trade_ideas.description: Long 20yr JGB on a 10s20s30s fly. Entry 73.5bps, target 50bps (revised), stop 66bps (revised).
trade_ideas.rationale: The fly has cheapened to levels that capped this cycle, the 20y has underperformed both wings, and ultra-long issuance has shifted down the curve.
trade_ideas.risk: A weak auction could change the direction of the super-long end, with fiscal concerns (Honebuto debate) unresolved.

tension_points.bull_case: A Knot presidency inside a package (France as Chief Economist, Germany keeping a Board seat) would probably be read as somewhat more hawkish at first, mainly at the front end.
tension_points.bear_case: A Dutch presidency with French and German appointments would leave Spain off the Executive Board, which could strengthen Hernández de Cos. Replacing Schnabel with a less hawkish voice would shift the balance dovishly even with Knot as President.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The composition of the full package, in particular who replaces Schnabel and who is named Chief Economist.

tension_points.bull_case: Continued Oman-mediated negotiations, no major new escalation and markets pricing reopening scenarios are bullish for risk and bearish for oil.
tension_points.bear_case: Iran keeps linking Hormuz reopening to broader political demands and shipping stays vulnerable even if headlines improve, which is bearish for risk and bullish for oil.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Brent sustained above $90/bbl with spikes above $100/bbl, or a Hormuz deal that sends Brent below $75/bbl.
